data.name: In Your Face TD
data.detailed_description:
In Your Face TD is a Tower Defense, which utilises room scale VR to give a new dimension to a classic genre.

You find yourself on a lonely space station, with only the mining drones to keep you company. Luckily the drones are hard workers, and they will gather resources so you can build defenses against invading creatures from another dimension.
These creatures are vicious, but they aren’t the brightest. They have one goal in mind, and that is destroying your base.
Smart as you are, you build a maze and lure the stupid creatures around and through your defences, before they can reach the base.
Knowing that space stations are regularly attacked by waves of evil, you've also brought your laser guns, bombs and even sawblade frisbees.

Features include:
  • Take advantage of the level design to build an optimal maze of towers and lure the enemies around your defences.
  • Take on the enemies face-to-face with three different weapons: Shotgun, laser minigun and sawblade frisbee.
  • Throw bombs at the enemies from the top of your towers.
  • Unlock upgrades based on your performance. Upgrades include chain-lightning, exploding sawblade frisbees, flying robot bombs and more.
  • Maximize your income by building mining drones.
  • Master the game on four difficulties ranging from Easy to Insane.

reviews.review:
In Your Face TD is a pretty unusual take on tower defense because I am not just sitting back and watching my towers do everything. The whole game is built around room scale VR, so I am standing inside a space station while creatures come through portals trying to destroy my base. I have to build defenses around the area, create routes for the enemies to follow and then get involved myself with weapons. I like that idea because it makes a familiar tower defense setup feel much more active.

The tower building is still important, and I like having to think about how I arrange everything. I can create a maze that sends the enemies through my defenses instead of simply putting towers wherever there is space. Mining drones also gather resources for me, so there is a small economy to manage while I am preparing for the next wave. The enemies are not especially complicated, but getting the layout right can make a big difference. I enjoy the feeling of watching a route I created actually work when a wave starts moving through it.

What makes the game stand out is the weapons. I can personally attack enemies with a shotgun, laser minigun and sawblade frisbee, while also throwing bombs from the top of towers. The sawblade is probably the funniest idea because it feels completely ridiculous in VR, but it also gives me something different to do instead of just waiting for the towers. There are upgrades as well, including chain lightning, exploding sawblades and flying robot bombs, so my defenses can become much more effective as I progress.

The VR presentation works well for the concept, although it also limits who can actually enjoy the game. I like being physically surrounded by the battlefield and being able to look around while enemies are moving through the maze. It makes the tower defense mechanics feel more hands on than they normally would. At the same time, I think the game can feel a little awkward when I am trying to manage the larger battlefield from inside it. A traditional tower defense game gives me a much easier overview of everything at once, while here I have to physically look around and move between different parts of the station.

The biggest weakness for me is the limited depth. There are four difficulty levels ranging from Easy to Insane, and the upgrade system gives me some progression, but the basic structure does not change very much. I am still building a maze, gathering resources, shooting enemies and surviving waves. Once I understand the best way to arrange my defenses, there is not a huge amount of variety to keep surprising me. I think more enemy types, maps and tower options would have helped the game stay interesting for longer.

I also think the game feels very much like an older VR experiment rather than a huge tower defense experience. The graphics are functional and the setting does its job, but I am here mainly for the unusual gameplay idea. That is not necessarily a bad thing because the game is free and the developers clearly wanted to experiment with how VR could change a familiar genre. I just have to keep my expectations reasonable. It is more of a compact arcade style tower defense than something I would spend dozens of hours mastering.

Overall, In Your Face TD is a fun little VR experiment that does enough differently to stand out. I like building enemy mazes, managing mining drones, personally fighting with the weapons and using upgrades to strengthen my defenses. The limited variety and slightly awkward battlefield management stop it from being a truly great tower defense game, but the fact that I can actually stand inside the action gives it a charm that a normal version would not have. For a free game, I think it is worth trying if I already have the right VR setup and want something short, simple and a little different.

Rating: 7.5/10
